newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE BUNDLED OUT FOR 141.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE BUNDLED OUT FOR 141.

text.p: Sri Lanka spinners Muthiah Muralitharan and Jayantha Silva engineered a remarkable batting collapse, capturing four wickets each as Zimbabwe were dismissed for 141 at tea on the first day of the second test on Wednesday.
Zimbabwe, who at one stage were on 119-2, lost their last eight wickets for 22 in a feeble display.
Skipper Alistair Campbell had to take a major share of the blame for starting the batting collapse.
Zimbabwe were cruising along merrily after Campbell had won the toss and decided to bat first on another grassless pitch, which did, however, possess bounce.
Campbell had put on 65 for the third wicket in 88 minutes with Grant Flower when the Zimbabwe captain lost his cool and jumped out to drive Silva.
Campbell missed the line and was stumped by Romesh Kaluwitharana yards out of his crease, for a well compiled 36. That irresponsible stroke cost Zimbabwe plenty.
In the next hour, the rest of the batsmen were all back in the pavilion with none of them reaching double figures.
Top scorer Grant Flower's innings of 52 in nearly three hours of solid defence was ended by Muralitharan who had him caught by Roshan Mahanama at slip. Flower hit six fours.
Muralitharan finished with 4 for 40 off 20 overs and Silva 4 for 16 off 10.1 overs.
The same pair had been responsible for Zimbabwe's innings defeat in the first test, capturing 14 wickets between them.
